title: A policy framed as relief for ordinary people turns benefits for organized private interests into politically defensible policy
body:
- A policy presented as populist economic relief can simultaneously restructure markets to deliver concentrated gains to specific industries.
- The populist framing makes the measure politically defensible while the material benefits accrue to organized private interests rather than the voters the policy claims to help.
- The same moral framing can be turned against competing rent-seeking sectors, letting one organized private interest attack another's market position under cover of consumer protection.
- Case: Credit card rate caps framed as consumer protection restructured markets to favor housing and construction, and the "Real Estate Cartel" used the same consumer-protection framing to attack competing unsecured-lending sectors.
conversion: A measure that serves organized private interests becomes politically defensible when it is framed as relief for ordinary people.
